lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Momentum was there, then Darren Raddysh threw it over the boards. The Maple Leafs' 3-2 loss to the Mammoth turned on Raddysh's late cross-checking penalty, with Nick Schmaltz converting the ensuing power play for the winner. Toronto had rallied from a sluggish start and briefly seized control, but coach Jim Hiller called the infraction what it was: a stupid penalty that cost them. That is the uncomfortable portrait of an 8-7 club sitting seventh in the Eastern Conference with 18 points - good enough to remain in the hunt, not consistent enough to command it. John Tavares offers the brighter note, upgraded to day-to-day after skating in a non-contact jersey, though he missed Tuesday's game. The Leafs now carry a one-game losing streak into Saturday's 7 p.m. meeting with Montreal. Watch Tavares' progress - and whether Toronto can stop turning winnable nights into self-inflicted wounds.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' offseason began with a resignation, not a splash - and that is fitting for a club that needs sharper direction before it needs another headline. David Bell has stepped down as assistant general manager and vice-president of baseball operations, leaving Toronto with another front-office vacancy and a mandate to reassess how it builds the roster. The 79-83 finish, second in the AL East, is merely the backdrop; the real work is replacing outfield production, reinforcing the rotation and deciding which expensive bets still deserve another roll. Bowden Francis, recently reinstated from the 60-day injured list, is a key piece to evaluate, while Ricky Tiedemann's health and the progress of left-hander Adam Macko will shape the pitching picture. In Arizona, a healthy Ricky Tiedemann has rediscovered his joy for baseball - a welcome sign, but not yet a solution. Watch the general managers meetings Nov. 9-12: Toronto's next direction should become visible there.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors are learning how to win without their biggest name - and doing it the hard way. Toronto erased a 16-point deficit and detonated for a 47-point fourth quarter Monday, beating the Clippers 125-118 while Kawhi Leonard watched from the sidelines. That comeback followed losses to the Lakers and Magic, leaving Toronto 4-3, third in the Atlantic Division, two and a half games back, but carrying a one-game winning streak into the night. Leonard's knee remains the central plot: he has completed treatment for left-knee swelling and begun the return-to-play process, with an update due in one week. Until then, the Raptors need their supporting cast to keep producing - and to avoid another collapse like the 131-125 loss to Los Angeles. Denver is next tonight at 9 p.m. ET, a stern road test of whether Monday's rally was a turning point or merely a rescue.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The victory restored the pulse, but it also exposed the price of staying alive. Washington's 27-10 dismantling of Philadelphia on Nov. 1 pushed the Commanders to 2-4-1, kept them second in the NFC East and snapped the season into a one-game winning streak. Now comes the bill: Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols are headed to injured reserve, with Payne lost for the season after a foot injury and Kinlaw sidelined at least four games. That strips the interior of the defense just as Washington must clean up its maddening pre-snap penalties - self-inflicted wounds that turn control into chaos. The Eagles win was convincing, but two games behind in the division leaves no room for sloppiness. Sunday's 1 p.m. ET meeting with the Rams is the next test: can a battered defensive front preserve the momentum without giving Los Angeles free yards?

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose to Mammoth on Late Goal
paragraphs: The Maple Leafs fell 3-2 to the Utah Mammoth on Tuesday, with Nick Schmaltz scoring the late power-play winner. Jack Roslovic scored both Toronto goals, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 33 shots. The Leafs are 8-7 and next face the Canadiens Saturday at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet.

The Blue Jays are looking ahead, with prospect Adam Macko Barriera saying he is enjoying baseball again while pitching in the Arizona Fall League. David Bell has also stepped down from his front-office roles. The Raptors visit Denver tonight at 9:00 p.m. ET, without Kawhi Leonard and Noah Bittle; Jakob Poeltl is day to day with a shoulder issue. Washington placed Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve. The Commanders host the Rams Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox.
